svg.text: What changed, what it cost, what comes next — and the same action billed to four other psyches
GRAYSCALE STRUCTURE WIREFRAME — no colour, no final type, no motion

g.text: THE CREDIT THIEF · RESOLVED · SESSION BEAT 20
You corrected the record — now, with evidence.
The room reorganizes around the correction. It lands, and it is cold. Two people message you afterwards; neither is your manager.
A · WHAT CHANGED — BEFORE → AFTER, PER FUNCTION
absorbed the routed Te work; did it in Ti’s manner — checkable, cold
took the timing decision; the pause was the window and it used it
stood down — its forecast was already correct, so it cost little
paid for the room. Nine people, tense-polite, and no capacity to hold it
thin bar = before · thick bar = after. Direction is stated with an explicit sign, never implied by bar direction alone.
B · WHAT IT COST — THE ITEMISED BILL
a live room is Se’s food
nine people is a full room
RUN THIS AGAIN ON ANOTHER PSYCHE
Same scenario, same action, different stack. The
counterfactual below is the whole pedagogical
This vessel carries its wear forward. It will not
Spend beats doing nothing. Stress decays; capacity
returns slowly; debt does not clear itself.
Discard session history and start from full capacity.
D · THE COUNTERFACTUAL — THE SAME ACTION, BILLED TO A DIFFERENT PSYCHE
Anything is doable. The bill varies. The bill predicts behaviour.
Fe pays 30 — but to keep the room, not to correct it
Every one of the four performed the identical action. None of them was blocked. What differed was who paid, how much, and how likely they were to have chosen it unforced.

svg.text: CALLOUT LEGEND — WHAT THE REGION DOES · HOV ON HOVER · CMT ON COMMIT · L/G UNDER LOOP OR GRIP
The outcome, in the scenario’s own voice
One sentence of authored consequence, plus a second sentence of aftermath. It is prose, not a metric, because the
user needs to know what happened in the world before they read what it cost inside.
Written once at commit and frozen.
Loop and Grip have their own outcome variants for the same action.
The transition is stated with the number that caused it: aggregate stress 41 → 58, crossing the 55 threshold. A
state change never happens without the screen saying which quantity crossed which line.
Fires here, after the receipt is computed.
A transition into Loop or Grip routes the “next” panel to the alleviate/aggravate deck instead of the normal one.
Four functions, four readouts each, thin bar for before and thick bar for after, with an explicit signed delta.
This is the only screen that shows before and after simultaneously; everywhere else, before is history and after
Hovering a function opens its full Reaction Window (S5) inline.
Under Loop the bypassed function shows a flat before/after pair and a “not consulted” note.
Every multiplier that touched the number, in the order the engine applied them: base cost, then per-function share
× rank, then the scenario’s context gate, then routing surcharge, then the relation multiplier. Nothing is
aggregated before the user has seen its parts.
Hovering a line highlights the function row it belongs to.
Loop and Grip multipliers appear as additional lines, tagged with the state that caused them.
Both distance-to-break meters restated with their before values in parentheses. This is where an action that felt
free reveals that it moved the psyche 13 points closer to a loop.
A crossed margin reads IN and the panel routes to the state’s own resolution copy.
The strongest affordance on the screen is “run this again on another psyche,” not “next scenario.” The product’s
thesis is comparative: one receipt teaches almost nothing, two receipts for the same action teach the whole model.
Previews the type picker with the current scenario and action preserved.
Re-runs the identical action on a fresh vessel of the chosen type.
The same action, priced against four different stacks, with the same four measures in the same positions. Bars are
comparable across cards because every card uses an identical scale.
Hovering a card expands its own itemised bill in place.
Selecting a card re-runs the scenario on that type.
Counterfactual vessels are always fresh, so the comparison is not contaminated by the current vessel’s wear.
One line per type naming which function absorbed the cost. This is the sentence most likely to produce the
intended realisation: the same visible behaviour was cheap for one psyche and ruinous for another, and the
difference was position in the stack.
Four figures: energy spent against the whole reservoir, stress added after peak-weighted aggregation, pleasure
after its conflict discount, and debt. Each names its method inline so the user is never asked to trust an
Debt is the figure that most often explains why the next run behaves badly.
A single closing line. It appears only here, at the end of a run, when the user has just watched the mechanism
The Te → Ti translation appears as its own line with its own multiplier, not folded into the base. A user must be
able to see that demanding a function you do not carry is not impossible, merely surcharged, and that the work
still got done in a different manner.
Doing nothing is offered as a real, selectable move with its own stated mechanics — stress decays, capacity
returns slowly, debt does not clear itself. Recovery is a state in the machine (D3), not an absence of activity.
Previews how many beats recovery would take at the current decay rates.
Advances beats without an action; each beat applies decay only.
From Grip, this is often the only affordable path.

Structure phase, grayscale by discipline. Colour, type scale, glyph artwork and motion curves are deferred to the visual-design phase; tick tuning, persistence and the text corpus are deferred to implementation. Both deferral lists are
enumerated in 00-BRIEF.md section 5 and BUILD-SPEC.md section 9. Worked type: ISTP (Ti / Se / Ni / Fe). Worked scenario: The Credit Thief.
